rationale: The umbrella root remains a non-Git routing workspace. Formal repositories are bitty, bitty-docs, bitty-website, bitty-devtools, bitty-mcp, bitty-plugin-sdk, and bitty-plugin-template under github.com/bitty-terminal; bitty-plugins is only a local grouping directory.
title: Use independent public repositories under bitty-terminal

consequences: The initial implementation must satisfy parser, plugin, IPC, recovery, fuzzing, and supply-chain gates before normal-use claims.
context: Bitty will parse untrusted PTY protocols and expose plugins, IPC, MCP, DevTools, clipboard, files, processes, and package updates.
decision_body: Every cross-boundary request must pass a granular policy, capability, authenticated scope, and resource budget as applicable; Terminal Truth remains core-owned and safe mode remains available.
rationale: Adding ambient authority or unbounded protocol APIs first would create ecosystem compatibility that later sandboxing could not safely retract.
title: Make security boundaries architectural P0 gates

consequences: All current risks remain Open and future tasks must link evidence before marking them mitigated.
context: The repository is being founded before product code exists and security controls have no implementation evidence.
decision_body: Security documents use normative requirements while explicitly marking every control unimplemented; implementation status changes require tests and independent review.
rationale: This prevents aspirational architecture from being reported as shipped behavior and keeps risks auditable.
title: Treat docs as pre-implementation contracts

rationale: Shared conversation mixes user-confirmed directions with assistant recommendations. Documents therefore label accepted working directions, candidate proposals, normative security contracts, open questions, and unimplemented status separately; silence after a suggestion is not treated as implementation evidence.
title: Use explicit decision-state taxonomy in foundation docs

rationale: The umbrella and bitty-plugins directories are local non-Git routing/grouping boundaries; seven public child remotes exist and are empty. Organization polyrepo is accepted, while the internal Cargo workspace and crate map remain candidates pending ADR.
title: Keep polyrepo facts separate from candidate core structure

rationale: core-boundaries and technology-strategy summarize ownership only and link to docs/security/overview.md, threat-model.md, and risk-register.md. Per-plugin VM, restricted Lua libraries, granular capabilities, protocol/graphics limits, budgets, safe mode, and read-only Agent defaults are normative but unimplemented P0 gates.
title: Use security documents as the P0 authority

rationale: Ghostty, Neovim, kitty, and WezTerm are pinned by local commit for reproducible study. Their presence does not select dependencies, create a fork commitment, or grant permission to execute cloned code.
title: Record reference clones as research snapshots

consequences: RichBlock, SemanticZone, scene primitives, structured transport, and protocol syntax remain candidate contracts; ordinary plugins receive no terminal-state mutation path.
context: Shared conversation turns 9-12 asked whether plugins can transform TUI and streaming Markdown output.
decision_body: Document Terminal State and VT/grid semantics as core-owned truth; plugins contribute constrained presentation, rich content, and overlays without rewriting PTY bytes or mutating the grid.
rationale: This preserves TUI cursor/mouse geometry, compatibility, copy/replay semantics, deterministic ownership, and the repository security invariants.
title: Preserve Terminal Truth across plugin presentation

consequences: CLI and hand editing can target one declarative desired-state model; install executes no package code, capability increases block update, and exact file/schema choices remain open.
context: Turns 15-18 require Lua customization plus first-party and third-party plugin lifecycle management.
decision_body: Keep Lua as the accepted user configuration language while documenting managed package manifest, exact lock, package store, resolver, and two-stage ConfigPlan details as candidates pending ADRs.
rationale: A package tool cannot safely rewrite arbitrary Lua, and source provenance does not justify promoting assistant-proposed file names or reconcile APIs to accepted contract.
title: Separate package lifecycle from Lua behavior configuration

consequences: All canonical Markdown must contain no CJK text. Historical source titles are represented by clear English descriptions rather than parallel-language copies.
context: The pre-implementation corpus needs one authoritative language before website routing and localization infrastructure exist.
decision_body: Maintain the current canonical corpus in English only. Defer i18n, translations, and locale routing until a future reviewed ADR explicitly reopens them.
rationale: A single canonical language prevents divergent contracts during the documentation-foundation phase while preserving a clear future decision point.
title: English is the only canonical documentation language

consequences: The synchronization, versioning, route mapping, publishing, and redirect mechanism remains unimplemented and requires the open docs-to-website ADR tracked as OQ-023.
context: The future Astro website needs an authoritative content origin without duplicating design contracts or implying that publishing integration already exists.
decision_body: Treat bitty-docs Markdown plus validated flat metadata as the canonical content source for future website publication.
rationale: Keeping contract content in bitty-docs avoids competing sources of truth and makes future publication eligibility explicit through metadata.
title: Validated bitty-docs Markdown is the future website content source

consequences: Technology documentation lists scaffolding and Rust edition 2024 as accepted; Cargo workspace details, dependencies, MSRV, nightly use, profiles, and concrete CI tiers remain undecided.
context: The project is completing documentation and governance before beginning basic repository, toolchain, and CI setup.
decision_body: Basic repository, toolchain, and CI scaffolding is authorized initialization work, and Rust components use edition 2024. CTX-0007 records the direction but does not implement scaffolding or select concrete dependencies.
rationale: This captures the user's explicit initialization boundary while preserving ADR and prototype gates for dependency choices.
title: Accept basic scaffolding and Rust edition 2024 for initialization

consequences: All existing docs require English translation and metadata; CI fails on CJK, malformed metadata, or title/H1 mismatch. Any future i18n or schema change needs a reviewed cross-repository decision and coordinated migration.
context: bitty-docs must remain maintainable as the source consumed by an independent website while product behavior is still pre-implementation.
decision_body: English is the sole canonical Markdown language for now. Every docs/**/*.md file uses exactly eight ordered flat scalar fields: title, description, category, audience, document_type, status, website_publish, and sidebar_order. The website consumes only website_publish true content from an immutable pinned docs revision; i18n and locale routing are deferred.
rationale: One language and a small deterministic schema prevent translation drift, make repository checks possible, and are compatible with schema-validated Markdown content collections without committing the website to a theme or sync mechanism.
title: Use English-only canonical docs with flat website metadata

consequences: Tasks remain open when affected documentation is stale. Post-initialization parallel work uses branches/worktrees and linked PRs; the shared-checkout exception ends after the first commit.
context: GitHub collaboration and CarryCtx durable coordination need one lifecycle, including a temporary exception for unborn repositories.
decision_body: Use Issue -> CarryCtx task -> branch/worktree -> commit -> PR -> independent review plus CI -> merge -> Issue closure and final checkpoint/completion. CarryCtx records team, dependencies, scopes, session, progress, checkpoints, handoffs, and acceptance. Documentation synchronization is required for completion. Before the first commit only, the commander may use a disjoint-scope shared checkout with CI-equivalent local checks.
rationale: The mapping keeps external collaboration, local durable state, isolation, review, and documentation evidence aligned while acknowledging that normal Git worktrees and PRs cannot exist before repository initialization.
title: Make independent delivery and synchronized docs the definition of done

consequences: Seven owned documents use website_publish true; the two internal project inventories use false while remaining canonical repository documents.
context: The website metadata requires an explicit publication decision for every translated document.
decision_body: Publish the product vision, architecture documents, security corpus, and technology strategy. Keep reference-projects.md and repository-map.md unpublished because they contain local clone paths, pinned research snapshots, workspace routing, and bootstrap inventory rather than durable public product guidance.
rationale: Public documentation should expose stable product and technical contracts without turning local operational inventory into website content.
title: Publish durable technical guidance but keep local inventories internal

consequences: Later implementation tasks pin concrete versions and lockfiles. Final crate graph, MSRV, dependencies, release policy, license, publication, automation, and website adapter/loader/theme/routes remain deferred; documentation alone is not implementation or deployment evidence.
context: The unborn Core and website repositories need reproducible checks and a deployable static shell before product implementation, without prematurely choosing final architecture, dependencies, or docs integration.
decision_body: Accept ADR 0001: Core uses a zero-functionality Rust 2024 resolver-3 workspace with dependency-free non-publishable bitty-core and bitty-app packages, stable rustfmt/clippy, just, and read-only fmt/clippy/test/actionlint CI. Website uses an Astro/Bun static shell producing dist and Cloudflare Workers Static Assets deployment with no adapter, Worker script, or docs consumer. CD references only CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN and CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID through GitHub secrets; CRATES_TOKEN remains unused.
rationale: This establishes testable initialization and current Cloudflare-recommended static deployment while preserving every product, dependency, publication, routing, and content-consumption decision for separate reviewed work.
title: Accept the implementation-neutral repository bootstrap baseline

rationale: Independent implementer (bitty-curator) fixed sidebar_order dedupe (specifications now 10/11/12/13), linked compat-RFC Tier-1 wording to ADR-0002, deferred ADR-0003 Input/Text crate placement via open bullets, repaired p0-acceptance-criteria traceability (bogus T-14 citation dropped, AC-025 R-014 added, 'enforced'->'normative'), and completed index/adrs-README listings. Commander re-ran all four gates (67 files, 0 issues). All six drafts remain proposed/draft awaiting project-initiator review.
title: Draft-batch revision round accepted via CTX-0023

rationale: Interactive HTML canvas visualizations using Konva and Fabric architectural patterns provide direct pan, zoom, node drag, layer filtering, flow stepping, and component inspection while preserving glossary.yaml as single source of truth and operating zero external network dependencies offline.
title: Migrate architecture diagrams from static placeholders to interactive HTML models

consequences: SDK R-SDK-1 can generate bitty.d.lua from this surface after acceptance; core-boundaries authority statement and Plugin Platform RFC namespace section need same-change updates on acceptance; 12 open questions recorded (authority placement, command metadata, service provider side, snapshot schema, observation identity, tasks/timers).
context: Plugin Platform RFC namespace block is explicitly illustrative and defers final spelling to core+SDK; Lua Runtime RFC fixes the versioned bitty bridge module; ADR-0006 already accepts bitty.env.get/has. Conflicts: FIND-0003 bitty.api.*, PX-1199/FIND-0003 register_panel/on_event/get_terminal_state, and draft plugin-reuse colon style bitty.services:get. Rust bitty-plugin-host has no Lua bridge; EventKind is a closed 17-name set; commands are manifest lazy QualifiedName reservations only.
decision_body: Adopt module root 'bitty' with namespaced functions from the accepted illustrative block (commands.register, events.subscribe, ui.mount/update, services.get, terminal.snapshot, settings.*, store.*, notify.show) plus accepted env.*. Reject bitty.api alias, flat verbs, colon style, and panel provider registration in v1. Event names equal the Rust EventKind closed set; payload shapes proposed from EventPayload/HostObservation. RFC marked draft; acceptance is a project decision.
rationale: Only the namespaced bitty.* shapes have accepted per-namespace rules and an accepted precedent (bitty.env.*). register_panel pre-empts the pending Panel RFC (Workspace Compositor introduces no PanelId; roadmap places panel providers post-1.0). One spelling per concept avoids compatibility ambiguity.
title: Plugin API v1 Lua surface: adopt bitty.<namespace> shapes; reject bitty.api and register_panel for v1

consequences: SDK defs/lint and template R-TPL-1 may derive from ADR-0009; bitty host bridge still needs its own task; RC-11 store quota is now part of the isolation ceiling set.
context: PR #186 (head 41c7274, CTX-0144) carried the Proposed ADR resolving the twelve open questions of the merged Plugin API v1 Lua Surface RFC draft (05ccdd9, CTX-0143). Issue #185 acceptance criteria required project ratification and a separate sync change before merge.
decision_body: Project initiator (user) ratified all twelve LUA-OQ resolutions exactly as proposed. ADR 0009 flipped draft to accepted; Plugin API v1 Lua Surface RFC flipped draft to accepted with a ratification note pointing at ADR 0009. Authority split recorded: bitty-docs owns the contract, bitty owns implementation/parity, SDK is generated. Acceptance-effects sync applied in the same change: plugin-platform-rfc identity/host-namespace/manifest-schema/disposal wording, core-boundaries authority sentence and semantic examples, ADR 0006 (LUA-OQ-2 note) and ADR 0007 (LUA-OQ-9 reconciliation note), Isolation Resource RFC RC-11, specifications index/decision register/ADR index/open-question OQ-011 row. R-SDK-1/R-SDK-2/R-SDK-3/R-TPL-1 and the bitty host-bridge work are unblocked but keep their own scoped tasks; no implementation is authorized by this docs change.
rationale: The owner approved the proposal wholesale; each row was verified against accepted sources (ADR 0006 typed denials, CLI Contract schema model, registry identity tuple, config chord grammar, RichBlock versioning, RC ceilings).
title: Ratify ADR 0009: accept Plugin API v1 Lua surface (LUA-OQ-1..12)
